title: Bicep Modules and Environments
description: Split a growing Bicep template into reusable modules and drive each environment from a parameter file.

data.text: A single 1,400-line Bicep file now deploys App Service, SQL, Storage, Key Vault, Application Insights, and three role assignments. Dev and production differ only by SKU names and a handful of settings, but someone duplicated the whole file with a `-prod` suffix. Refactor it.

Extract one **Bicep module per concern** (`modules/app-service.bicep`, `modules/sql.bicep`, `modules/monitoring.bicep`) each with a typed `param`/`output` contract. Keep one entry template per environment that composes the modules and reads environment-specific values from a **`.bicepparam` parameter file**. Never branch environment logic with long inline `if` chains inside a shared file.

data.title: modules/app-service.bicep — typed contract
main.prod.bicepparam — environment values only
data.code:
using './main.bicep'

param environment = 'prod'
param location = 'westeurope'
param appServiceSku = 'P1v3'
param sqlSku = 'S3'
param alertEmail = 'oncall@example.com'

data.text: Duplicating a template means every fix must be applied twice and the copies silently diverge. A module contract also makes the blast radius explicit: reviewers see that `app-service.bicep` only touches `Microsoft.Web/*`, and typed `@allowed` parameters catch a typo in a SKU name at validation time instead of mid-deployment.
